extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involved three stages, beginning with the selection of 30 subjects across six disciplines based on the prevalence of visual inputs in common university majors. The subsequent stage involved recruiting annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from college-level exams, quizzes, and textbooks covering various disciplines.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources, and created new questions based on their expertise. Quality control involved three stages: 1) identifying duplicates using lexical overlap and URL similarity, 2) manual format and typo checking by co-authors, and 3) categorizing problems into four difficulty levels and excluding overly simplistic ones.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including the paper's co-authors, who specialize in the majors/subjects covered by the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases introduced during its manual curation process.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset's focus on college-level subjects may be insufficient for fully testing Expert AGI, and its manual curation process may introduce biases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed to be used as a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating and testing the capabilities of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in the context of Expert AGI.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57].

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The introduction of MMMU marks a significant step towards evaluating the capabilities of LMMs in the context of Expert AGI. By assessing both basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities across various professional domains, MMMU provides a comprehensive benchmark
